tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# OLMo-core 是什么：项目定位与全景图
2	
3	> 所属单元：单元一「初识 OLMo-core」（第 1 讲 / 共 4 讲）
4	> 难度：入门（beginner）
5	> 前置讲义：无（这是整个学习手册的第一篇）
6	
7	## 1. 本讲目标
8	
9	学完本讲，你应该能够：
10	
11	1. 用一句话说清 OLMo-core 是什么、由谁维护、用来做什么。
12	2. 说出 OLMo-core 在 OLMo 生态中的四个位置：**训练库本体、官方训练脚本、Docker/Beaker 镜像、推理与生态集成（Hugging Face / vLLM / 自带 chat）**。
13	3. 区分仓库里四个代码区域的不同职责：`src/olmo_core`（库源码）、`src/test`（测试）、`src/scripts`（脚本）、`src/examples`（示例）。
14	4. 说出常见可选依赖（flash-attn、ring-flash-attn、TransformerEngine、grouped_gemm、torchao、Liger-Kernel、QuACK）分别解锁哪些功能，并理解「核心轻量、功能按需安装」的设计哲学。
15	5. 完成第一个代码实践：通读 README，写出「用 OLMo-core 训练一个 190M 模型需要哪几个组件」的初步猜想（这份猜想会在第 4 讲验证）。
16	
17	## 2. 前置知识
18	
19	本讲几乎不需要写代码，但下面几个概念会让你读起来更顺畅：
20	
21	- **大语言模型（LLM）与预训练**：给模型喂海量文本，让它学会「预测下一个 token」。token 是文本切分后的最小单位，模型输入输出都是 token 序列。
22	- **Checkpoint（检查点）**：训练过程中保存的模型权重文件。发布一个模型，本质上是发布一组 checkpoint。
23	- **Transformer**：当前几乎所有 LLM 的基础网络结构，由注意力机制和前馈网络堆叠而成。OLMo 系列模型就是 Transformer。本讲不需要懂内部细节，第 3 单元会专门精读。
24	- **Python 包管理**：知道 `pip install`、`pyproject.toml` 是 Python 项目的依赖与元数据描述文件即可。
25	- **git 与 GitHub**：会 `git clone`、能在 GitHub 上打开文件链接即可。本讲的所有「永久链接」都指向 GitHub 上固定 commit 的源码。
26	- **GPU**：本讲完全不需要 GPU；整个手册中只有部分实践任务需要（届时会明确标注）。
27	
28	一些名词解释：
29	
30	| 术语 | 含义 |
31	|------|------|
32	| AI2 | Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence（艾伦人工智能研究所），OLMo 系列模型的发布方 |
33	| OLMo | Open Language Model，AI2 的开源大模型系列（OLMo-1/2/3、OLMoE、Molmo 等） |
34	| Beaker | AI2 内部的集群实验平台，类似内部的「云训练平台」 |
35	| torchrun | PyTorch 自带的多进程启动器，用来启动多 GPU 训练 |

52	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
53	
54	本讲拆成 3 个最小模块：
55	
56	- 4.1 OLMo-core 的定位与生态位
57	- 4.2 OLMo-core 提供的四类能力
58	- 4.3 仓库四大区域与可选依赖
59	
60	### 4.1 OLMo-core 的定位与生态位
61	
62	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
63	
64	打开仓库首页，README 的标题区只有一句话副标题：
65	
66	> **Building blocks for OLMo modeling and training**（OLMo 建模与训练的积木）
67	
68	这句话就是定位：OLMo-core **不是一个模型，而是一个训练库**。它提供搭一台「语言模型训练机器」所需的全部零件——模型结构、数据加载、优化器、训练循环、分布式并行、评测与生成——让你像搭积木一样组装出一次训练实验。
69	
70	它与生态中其他角色的分工：
71	
72	| 角色 | 是什么 | 在哪 |
73	|------|--------|------|
74	| OLMo 模型权重 | 已训练好的模型 checkpoint（如 `allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B`） | Hugging Face Hub |
75	| **OLMo-core** | **训练这些模型的库（本手册主角）** | GitHub `allenai/OLMo-core` / PyPI `ai2-olmo-core` |
76	| OLMo Eval、olmes | 评测工具 | 独立仓库 `allenai/OLMo-eval`、`allenai/olmes` |
77	| OLMo 论文 | 训练方法与结果的学术记录（如《2 OLMo 2 Furious》） | arXiv |
78	
79	一个常见的误解是「OLMo-core = OLMo 模型」。更准确的说法是：**OLMo 模型是 OLMo-core 跑出来的产物**。官方发布 OLMo-2 32B、OLMo-3 7B/32B 时，同时在这仓库里公开了复现实验的完整训练脚本（4.2 会讲）。
80	
81	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
82	
83	用一张文字版生态图理解数据与代码怎么流动：
84	
85	```text
86	                    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
87	                    │              OLMo-core（库）                │
88	                    │  模型结构 · 数据加载 · 优化器 · 训练循环      │
89	                    │  分布式并行 · 评测 · 生成                    │
90	                    └──────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
91	                                   │ 官方脚本组装成完整实验
92	                    ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐
93	                    │ src/scripts/official/ 训练脚本│
94	                    └──────────────┬──────────────┘
95	              torchrun 本地启动    │      Beaker/Gantry + Docker 镜像集群启动
96	                    ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐
97	                    │   训练产出：checkpoint 权重    │
98	                    └──────────────┬──────────────┘
99	                                   │ 转换 / 发布
100	              ┌────────────────────┼────────────────────┐
101	              ▼                    ▼                     ▼
102	      HF transformers 推理      vLLM 高吞吐推理    OLMo Eval / olmes 评测
103	              └──────────── 用户使用模型 ────────────────┘
104	```
105	
106	也就是说：OLMo-core 站在生态的「生产侧」，而 HF/vLLM/评测工具站在「消费侧」。
107

It provides modular components for transformer architectures, distributed training, data loading, and evaluation.」* 这四块（模型结构、分布式训练、数据加载、评测）正是学习手册第 3–8 单元的骨架。

143	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
144	
145	**练习 1**：OLMo-core 和 OLMo 模型是什么关系？
146	
147	> **答案**：OLMo 模型是 checkpoint（一组训练好的权重），发布在 Hugging Face Hub；OLMo-core 是训练这些权重的 Python 库，提供模型结构、数据、优化器、训练循环等组件。关系是「工厂与产品」。
148	
149	**练习 2**：如果你只想用 OLMo-3 模型做推理，需要安装 OLMo-core 吗？
150	
151	> **答案**：不需要。README 的 Inference 一节（[README.md:101-151](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L101-L151)）显示只需 `transformers` 或 `vllm` 即可加载 `allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B` 推理。OLMo-core 只有在你想用自己的方式做生成实验（beta 的 chat demo）或训练/微调时才需要。
152	
153	**练习 3**：项目在哪里声明「当前活跃开发的方向」？举一个证据。
154	
155	> **答案**：CHANGELOG.md 的 `Unreleased` 段（[CHANGELOG.md:8-27](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/CHANGELOG.md#L8-L27)）。例如其中记录了新增 `olmo_core.nn.maxtext`（与 MaxText 互转 checkpoint）和 `olmo_core.data.multimodal`（Molmo2 多模态数据核心），说明近期方向是多模态与生态互转。
156	
157	### 4.2 OLMo-core 提供的四类能力
158	
159	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
160	
161	把 README 通读一遍后，可以把 OLMo-core 对外提供的东西归纳为四类能力。这四类能力也正好对应四种典型用法：
162	
163	| 能力 | 是什么 | 典型用法 |
164	|------|--------|----------|
165	| ① 组件库 | `src/olmo_core` 里的可组合 Python 组件（模型、数据、优化器、训练循环…） | 像搭积木一样写自己的训练实验 |
166	| ② 官方训练脚本 | `src/scripts/official/` 下复现已发布模型的完整配方 | 一条 `torchrun` 命令复现 OLMo-2/3 训练 |
167	| ③ Docker 镜像 | 预装全部（含可选）依赖的 GPU 镜像 + Beaker 启动器 | 在集群上一键拉起多节点训练 |
168	| ④ 推理与生态集成 | 自带的自回归生成/chat（beta）、HF 权重互转脚本 | 加载 checkpoint 对话、把权重转成 HF 格式 |
169	
170	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
171	
172	四类能力组合起来的典型工作流（预训练一个模型的路径）：
173	
174	```text
175	选一个官方脚本（能力②）
176	    │  按硬件改配置（组件库的 Config 体系，能力①）
177	    ▼
178	在 Docker 镜像里用 Beaker/torchrun 启动（能力③）
179	    │  训练循环产出 checkpoint
180	    ▼
181	转成 HF 格式 / 用 chat demo 检查生成质量（能力④）
182	```
183	
184	关键理解：**能力②③是「打包好的一整套」，能力①是「散装零件」**。你可以直接跑官方配方，也可以只借某个零件（比如只用它的 MoE 模块或数据加载器）拼进自己的代码。
185	
186	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
187	
188	**① 组件库：安装即得**
189	
190	[README.md:32-47](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L32-L47) 给出两种安装方式：开发装 `pip install -e .[all]`（从源码、带全部可选依赖）或直接 `pip install ai2-olmo-core`。装好后 `import olmo_core` 拿到的就是组件库本体。
191	
192	**② 官方训练脚本：一条命令复现 32B 训练**
193	
194	[README.md:65-99](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L65-L99) 是官方脚本的完整用法说明，三个要点：
195	
196	- 用 `torchrun` 启动，例如 [README.md:74-76](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L74-L76) 的 `torchrun --nproc-per-node=8 src/scripts/official/OLMo2/OLMo-2-0325-32B-train.py --save-folder=...`；
197	- 绝大多数配置能用**点号路径**从命令行覆盖，例如 [README.md:81-84](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L81-L84) 用 `--train_module.optim.lr=6e-3` 改学习率（原理在第 2 单元讲）；
198	- 目前有 OLMo-2 与 OLMo-3 两个家族（[README.md:94-99](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L94-L99) 的表格）；仓库里实际还有 `OLMo-hybrid` 目录（用 `ls src/scripts/official/` 可验证）。
199	
200	配套的 [src/scripts/official/README.md:1-8](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/src/scripts/official/README.md#L1-L8) 补充了两个极实用的小技巧：给脚本加 `--help` 看必填参数，加 `--dry-run` 在不启动训练的情况下打印最终生效的完整配置。**这在没有 GPU 的机器上也能跑，是你后面每一讲的好帮手。**
201	
202	**③ Docker 镜像与 Beaker 启动**
203	
204	[README.md:57-63](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L57-L63) 说明了官方 Docker 镜像的两个重要约定：镜像包含**全部依赖但不包含 Olmo-core 本身**（源码在运行时 clone 进容器，方便代码频繁变更）；镜像在自家 H100 集群上定期测试，换硬件可能需要自己改 Dockerfile。
205	
206	启动机制在 [AGENTS.md:145-151](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/AGENTS.md#L145-L151)：`launch` 命令会生成一个 Gantry 配方，四步走——起容器 → clone 指定 commit 的仓库 → `pip install -e .` → 用 torchrun 跑训练命令。细节留到第 9 单元。
207	
208	**④ 推理与生态集成**
209	
210	- 自带生成（beta）：[README.md:153-159](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L153-L159) 的 `python -m olmo_core.generate.chat <checkpoint-url>` 可以直接跟一个 OLMo checkpoint 聊天；
211	- HF 权重互转：`src/examples/huggingface/` 下有双向转换脚本（`convert_checkpoint_to_hf.py` 等，第 10 单元精读）。
212	
213	#### 4.2.4 代码实践
214	
215	**实践：把「四类能力」各自落到一个具体入口**
216	
217	1. **实践目标**：不再抽象地背「四类能力」，而是为每类能力找到仓库里一个具体文件或一条具体命令。
218	2. **操作步骤**：
219	   - 能力①（组件库）：`ls src/olmo_core/`，记下你看到的子包名（应有 `nn`、`data`、`optim`、`train`、`distributed`、`eval`、`generate` 等）；
220	   - 能力②（官方脚本）：`ls src/scripts/official/`，再挑一个脚本文件打开，只看文件开头的 docstring 与 import，不看正文；
221	   - 能力③（镜像）：打开 [src/Dockerfile](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/src/Dockerfile) 看前 30 行，确认它是两阶段构建；
222	   - 能力④（推理集成）：在 README 里找到 chat demo 命令和 HF 互转脚本所在的 examples 目录。
223	3. **需要观察的现象**：每类能力都真实存在且入口明确；官方脚本 import 的几乎全是 `olmo_core.*` 里的 Config 类。
224	4. **预期结果**：得到一张「能力 → 入口文件」对照表（形如：组件库→`src/olmo_core/`、官方脚本→`src/scripts/official/OLMo3/…`、镜像→`src/Dockerfile`、推理→`olmo_core.generate.chat`）。
225	5. 以上全部是只读操作，不依赖 GPU；`--dry-run` 相关实验在第 9 单元再做。**待本地验证**（需要先完成第 2 讲的安装）。
226	
227	#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案
228	
229	**练习 1**：官方训练脚本为什么推荐用 `--dry-run` 先跑一遍？
230	
231	> **答案**：`--dry-run` 会打印合并命令行覆盖之后的**最终完整配置**但不真正启动训练（见 [src/scripts/official/README.md:1-8](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/src/scripts/official/README.md#L1-L8)）。这样可以在花 GPU 时间之前检查配置是否正确，也让我们这些学习者能零成本研究一份完整训练配方长什么样。
232	
233	**练习 2**：官方 Docker 镜像里为什么不预装 Olmo-core 包本身？
234	
235	> **答案**：[README.md:60](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L60) 说明这是为了适应频繁的代码变更——镜像只锁依赖，源码在任务启动时按指定 commit clone 并 `pip install -e .`。这样改代码不需要重打镜像。

240	
241	### 4.3 仓库四大区域与可选依赖
242	
243	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
244	
245	**四大区域**。仓库的 `src/` 下按职责分成四块（[README.md:165-174](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L165-L174) 的 Development 一节点名了前两块）：
246	
247	| 区域 | 职责 | 你什么时候会去 |
248	|------|------|----------------|
249	| `src/olmo_core/` | 库本体：所有可 import 的组件 | 几乎每一讲 |
250	| `src/test/` | 测试，目录结构与库一一镜像 | 想确认某组件行为时（测试是最好的用法示例） |
251	| `src/scripts/` | 训练/工具脚本：`official/`（官方配方）、`train/`（内部模板）等 | 第 9 单元 |
252	| `src/examples/` | 自包含小示例：`llm/`、`moe/`、`huggingface/` 等 | 第 4 讲跑第一个例子 |
253	
254	`src/olmo_core/` 内部的子包按功能划分：`nn/`（模型结构）、`data/`（数据）、`optim/`（优化器）、`train/`（训练循环）、`distributed/`（并行与 checkpoint）、`eval/`（评测）、`generate/`（生成）、`launch/`（集群启动）、`kernels/`（自定义 CUDA 内核）、`float8/`（低精度训练）——这张「内景图」第 3 讲会详细展开。
255	
256	**可选依赖**。OLMo-core 的核心只要求 PyTorch，重度 GPU 功能按需挂载可选依赖（[README.md:49-55](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/README.md#L49-L55)）：
257	
258	| 可选依赖 | 解锁的功能 | 对应源码位置（证据） |
259	|----------|------------|----------------------|
260	| flash-attn | FlashAttention 注意力后端 | `src/olmo_core/nn/attention/flash_attn_api.py` |
261	| ring-flash-attn | 环形注意力（上下文并行）后端 | `src/olmo_core/nn/attention/ring.py`、`backend.py` |
262	| TransformerEngine | TE 注意力后端、mxfp8 相关内核 | `src/olmo_core/nn/attention/te_attn_api.py`、`src/olmo_core/kernels/mxfp8_utils.py` |
263	| Liger-Kernel | 低显存「fused-linear」损失实现 | README 说明；损失相关在模型侧 |
264	| torchao | float8 训练 | `src/olmo_core/float8/` |
265	| grouped_gemm | dropless MoE（混合专家）模型 | `src/olmo_core/nn/moe/mlp.py` 等 |
266	| QuACK | 部分 CuTe 内核 | `src/olmo_core/kernels/`、`src/olmo_core/ops/` |
267	
268	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
269	
270	「按需挂载」的实现模式是 Python 的 `try/except ImportError`：
271	
272	```text
273	import 某个可选库
274	    ├─ 成功 → 该功能可用（如 has_flash_attn_2() 返回 True）
275	    └─ 失败 → 模块置为 None，功能自动降级/禁用，其余部分照常工作
276	```
277	
278	好处是：装一个轻量版 OLMo-core 就能读代码、跑 CPU 测试、写配置；只有真正要训练大模型时才需要装齐 GPU 依赖。这也是为什么 `pip install -e .[all]` 里 `[all]` 会显著拉长安装时间——它把 `dev`、`beaker`、`fa4`、`fla`、`torchao`、`wandb` 等 extras 全部拉进来（见 [pyproject.toml:36-91](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/pyproject.toml#L36-L91)）。
279	
280	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
281	
282	**① 可选导入的标准写法**
283	
284	[src/olmo_core/nn/attention/flash_attn_api.py:9-32](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/src/olmo_core/nn/attention/flash_attn_api.py#L9-L32) 连续用四个 `try/except ImportError` 分别尝试导入 flash-attn 2、flash-attn 3（还有两种模块路径的回退）、flash-attn 4 和 ring-flash-attn，全部失败就置 `None`。这就是 4.3.2 流程图的真实代码。
285	
286	**② 能力探测函数**
287	
288	紧随其后的 [flash_attn_api.py:37-60](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/src/olmo_core/nn/attention/flash_attn_api.py#L37-L60) 定义了 `has_flash_attn_2()`、`has_flash_attn_3()`、`has_flash_attn_4()`：不仅检查「装没装」，还检查 GPU 架构是否匹配（例如 flash-attn 3 只认 H100/H800，flash-attn 4 认 Blackwell）。运行时靠这些函数决定选哪个后端——注意力后端的可插拔机制第 3 单元精读。
289	
290	**③ extras 的权威定义**
291	
292	[pyproject.toml:36-91](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/pyproject.toml#L36-L91) 定义了全部 extras。注意两点：`dev` 里是 pytest/black/ruff/mypy 等开发工具；`all`（[pyproject.toml:91](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/pyproject.toml#L91)）是其余 extras 的合集。README 提到的 grouped_gemm、ring-flash-attn、TransformerEngine 等不在 extras 里，需要按 README 指引自行安装（grouped_gemm 甚至可能要从源码编译）。
293	
294	**④ 测试镜像源码结构**
295	
296	[AGENTS.md:155-160](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/blob/2289b819b8f709e37e3e042ebb019f411fb6b742/AGENTS.md#L155-L160) 描述了测试约定：`src/test/` 镜像源码结构、测试函数命名 `test_*`、GPU 测试用 `@pytest.mark.gpu` 标记且无 GPU 时自动跳过。所以 `pytest -v src/` 在笔记本上也能跑——大部分重型测试会安静地 skip。

319	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
320	
321	**练习 1**：`pip install ai2-olmo-core` 之后，直接 `import olmo_core` 并构建一个普通（非 MoE、非 flash-attn）的 Transformer 模型，需要额外装 flash-attn 吗？
322	
323	> **答案**：不需要。flash-attn 只是**注意力后端之一**，未安装时该后端被禁用（`has_flash_attn_2()` 返回 False），模型可使用默认后端。只有 grouped_gemm 之于 MoE 这类「该功能的核心实现依赖它」的情况才必须装。
324	
325	**练习 2**：为什么 `src/test` 的目录结构与 `src/olmo_core` 镜对应？这对你读代码有什么用？
326	
327	> **答案**：镜像结构（如 `src/olmo_core/data/` 对应 `src/test/data/`）让「找某组件的测试」变成机械操作：把路径里的 `olmo_core` 换成 `test`。测试往往是组件最可靠的用法文档——比 docstring 更能说明输入输出和边界行为。
328	
329	**练习 3**：`pip install -e '.[all]'` 和 `pip install ai2-olmo-core` 的三个主要区别？
330	
331	> **答案**：① `-e` 从本地源码安装（可编辑，改代码立即生效）vs 从 PyPI 装快照；② `[all]` 附带全部 extras（开发工具、beaker、torchao、wandb 等）vs 只装核心依赖；③ 前者要求先 clone 仓库、适合开发，后者适合只做使用。

347	## 6. 本讲小结
348	
349	- OLMo-core 是 AI2 的 **OLMo 系列模型训练库**（PyPI 包名 `ai2-olmo-core`），提供「建模与训练的积木」；模型权重本身发布在 Hugging Face Hub。
350	- 它对外提供**四类能力**：可组合组件库（`src/olmo_core`）、官方训练脚本（`src/scripts/official`，可用 `--dry-run` 零成本查看完整配置）、Docker/Beaker 镜像与启动器、推理与生态集成（beta chat、HF 互转）。
351	- 仓库分四大区域：`src/olmo_core`（库）、`src/test`（镜像结构的测试）、`src/scripts`（脚本）、`src/examples`（示例）。
352	- 核心只依赖 PyTorch；flash-attn/ring-flash-attn/TransformerEngine/grouped_gemm/torchao 等可选依赖按需解锁注意力后端、MoE、float8 等功能，实现方式是 `try/except ImportError` 加 `has_*()` 探测函数。
353	- `--train_module.optim.lr=6e-3` 式的命令行覆盖预示了贯穿全库的「一切皆 Config」设计模式，这是第 2 单元的主题。

31 32 ## Installation 33 34 First install [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org) according to the instructions specific to your operating system and hardware. 35 36 For development, we recommend installing from source: 37 38 ```bash 39 git clone https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core.git 40 cd Olmo-core 41 pip install -e .[all] 42 ``` 43 Or you can install from PyPI with: 44 45 ```bash 46 pip install ai2-olmo-core 47 ``` 48 49 There are a number of optional dependencies that must be installed to use certain functionality as well, including: 50 51 - [flash-attn](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention), [ring-flash-attn](https://github.com/zhuzilin/ring-flash-attention), and [TransformerEngine](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine) for the corresponding attention backends. 52 - [Liger-Kernel](https://github.com/linkedin/Liger-Kernel) for a low-memory "fused-linear" loss implementation. 53 - [torchao](https://github.com/pytorch/ao) for float8 training. 54 - [grouped_gemm](https://github.com/tgale96/grouped_gemm) for dropless mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. You may need to compile from source until [PR #21](https://github.com/tgale96/grouped_gemm/pull/21) is released (post v0.1.6). 55 - [QuACK](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/quack) for some CuTe-based kernels. 56 57 The published [Docker images](https://github.com/orgs/allenai/packages?repo_name=Olmo-core) contain all core and optional dependencies, and are regularly tested on our in-house H100 clusters. 58 But there are several things to keep in mind if you intend to use these images: 59 60 - They do not come with the Olmo-core package installed, only its dependencies, to accommodate for regular code changes. 61 - They may not work on your own cluster if you have different hardware or driver/CUDA versions. 62 63 If the published images do not work for your use-case for any of the above reasons, you could adapt our [Dockerfile](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/blob/main/src/Dockerfile) to build your own images. 64 65 ## Official training scripts 66 67 Official training scripts for released models can be found in [`src/scripts/official/`](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/tree/main/src/scripts/official). 68 69 These scripts are meant to be launched with ``torchrun``, or with Olmo-core's Beaker launch CLI if you have access to Beaker. 70 71 For example: 72 73 ```bash 74 torchrun --nproc-per-node=8 src/scripts/official/OLMo2/OLMo-2-0325-32B-train.py \ 75 --save-folder=/path/to/save/checkpoints 76 ``` 77 78 You can override most configuration options from the command-line. For example, to override the learning rate you could launch the script like this: 79 80 ```bash 81 torchrun --nproc-per-node=8 src/scripts/official/OLMo2/OLMo-2-0325-32B-train.py \ 82 --save-folder=/path/to/save/checkpoints \ 83 --train_module.optim.lr=6e-3 84 ``` 85 86 To continue annealing from a checkpoint, we use a separate script which can be launched like this: 87 88 ```bash 89 torchrun --nproc-per-node=8 src/scripts/official/OLMo2/OLMo-2-0325-32B-anneal.py \ 90 --save-folder=/path/to/save/checkpoints \ 91 --checkpoint=https://storage.googleapis.com/ai2-llm/peteish32/step721901 92 ``` 93 94 ### Available Training Scripts 95 96 | Model Family | Directory | Description | 97 |--------------|-----------|-------------| 98 | **OLMo-2** | [`src/scripts/official/OLMo2/`](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/tree/main/src/scripts/official/OLMo2) | Training scripts and model card for OLMo-2 32B models | 99 | **OLMo-3** | [`src/scripts/official/OLMo3/`](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/tree/main/src/scripts/official/OLMo3) | Training scripts and model cards for OLMo-3 7B and 32B models | 100 101 ## Inference 102 103 ### With Hugging Face Transformers 104 105 You can use our Hugging Face [transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers) integration to run inference on the OLMo checkpoints: 106 107 ```bash 108 pip install transformers>=4.57.0 109 ``` 110 111 ```python 112 from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer 113 olmo = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B") 114 tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B") 115 message = ["Language modeling is "] 116 inputs = tokenizer(message, return_tensors='pt', return_token_type_ids=False) 117 # inputs = {k: v.to('cuda') for k,v in inputs.items()} # optional verifying cuda 118 # olmo = olmo.to('cuda') 119 response = olmo.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=100, do_sample=True, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.7) 120 print(tokenizer.batch_decode(response, skip_special_tokens=True)[0]) 121 ``` 122 123 Alternatively, with the Hugging Face pipeline abstraction: 124 125 ```python 126 from transformers import pipeline 127 olmo_pipe = pipeline("text-generation", model="allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B") 128 print(olmo_pipe("Language modeling is")) 129 ``` 130 131 ### With vLLM 132 133 [vLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/) provides high-throughput inference for OLMo models. You can use it for offline batched inference: 134 135 ```bash 136 pip install vllm>=0.11.0 137 ``` 138 139 ```python 140 from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams 141 llm = LLM(model="allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B") 142 sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, top_p=0.7) 143 prompts = ["Language modeling is"] 144 outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params) 145 for output in outputs: 146 prompt = output.prompt 147 generated_text = output.outputs[0].text 148 print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}, Generated text: {generated_text!r}") 149 ``` 150 151 For more details, see the [vLLM documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/quickstart/#offline-batched-inference). 152 153 ### With Olmo-core (beta) 154 155 Autoregressive generation is supported directly in Olmo-core. Using this capability, we provide a chat-loop demo that can be used to interact with models in an interactive chat session: 156 157 ```bash 158 python -m olmo_core.generate.chat https://olmo-checkpoints.org/ai2-llm/Olmo-3-1025-7B/stage3/step11921/ --max-new-tokens 512 159 ``` 160 161 ## Evaluation 162 163 Additional tools for evaluating OLMo models are available at the [OLMo Eval](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-eval) and [olmes](https://github.com/allenai/olmes) repositories. 164 165 ## Development 166 167 The Python library source code is located in `src/olmo_core`. The corresponding tests are located in `src/test`. The library docs are located in `docs`. You can build the docs locally with `make docs`. 168 169 Code checks: 170 171 - We use `pytest` to run tests. You can run all tests with `pytest -v src/test`. You can also point `pytest` at a specific test file to run it individually. 172 - We use `isort` and `black` for code formatting. 1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
6	and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
7	
8	## Unreleased
9	
10	### Added
11	
12	- Added `UnshardedModelExportCallback` and `load_unsharded_model_state()`, which write an unsharded `model.safetensors` (plus the config) into every permanent checkpoint so evaluation can read one file instead of the sharded state.
13	- Added the Molmo2 stage-1 pretraining recipe: the stage-1 datasets (PixMo-Cap, PixMo-Points/Count v1 and v2, CoSyn-Point, MolmoPoint-GUISyn, OCR caption tars / OlmOCR / synthetic OCR / text-rich captions, academic QA, PixMo-Clocks, Tulu 4 text) with their mixtures, and `src/scripts/train/Molmo2-Stage1.py` (`dry_run` / `launch` / `train`; v1/v2/v3 recipes, 4B and 8B).
14	- Added `olmo_core.nn.maxtext` for converting model weights between OLMo Core and MaxText checkpoints in both directions, built on `StateConverter` like the Hugging Face converter. It picks the MaxText decoder from the OLMo Core config (dense `olmo3`, and the hybrid KDA/MoE `olmoe3`), handles MaxText's scanned and unscanned layouts, and checks that converting back is bit-exact. Example CLIs are in `src/examples/maxtext/`.
15	- Added Molmo2 support in `olmo_core.nn.vision`: a HuggingFace Molmo2 checkpoint loader (`molmo2_loader`) and special-token definitions, plus logit-parity and generation tests. `MultimodalLM` gains bidirectional image-token attention (`token_type_ids`), explicit RoPE `position_ids`, and sub-segment (branch-packing) attention isolation.
16	- Added `MultimodalTransformerTrainModule` for training `MultimodalLM` (per-token weighted loss, optimizer param groups for the LM / vision tower / connector, FSDP/DDP over the composite model), `weighted_cross_entropy_loss`, the `PerGroupScheduler` (per-param-group LR schedules), and examples-per-second / extra-FLOPs reporting in `SpeedMonitorCallback`.
17	- Added the `olmo_core.data.multimodal` data core for Molmo2: multi-annotation (branch-packing) `build_packed_sequence` with float loss weights, `pack_examples`, `MultimodalCollator`, a weighted resumable `MixtureDataLoader`, the `SftFormatter` prompt formatter, message/weight utilities, the Molmo2 image preprocessor (`preprocess_image_molmo2`), and the `PixMoCapDataset` caption dataset.
18	- Added a FlexAttention backend supporting the bidirectional-image and sub-segment masks, `RoPE` `position_ids`, `SplitVocabEmbedding` / `TransformerConfig.n_extra_vocab` (separately freezable extra-token rows), `response_logits_only` for `LMHead`, and `masked_dropout` (per-token residual dropout) on `ResidualStream`.
19	- Added Ulysses context parallelism for `KimiDeltaAttention` (`apply_cp`), mirroring the `GatedDeltaNet` all-to-all head/sequence exchange, with the in-kernel gate parameters sliced to each rank's heads.
20	- Added a Ulysses context-parallel parity test for the recurrent mixers (`GatedDeltaNet`, `KimiDeltaAttention`) that compares per-stage activations, outputs, and gradients against a single-process reference, including packed documents that straddle the CP split, plus a model-level gradient-parity test for `gdn` and `kda` under Ulysses CP.
21	- Added opt-in router replay and current-policy balancing counts, custom training objectives,
22	  bounded checkpoint planning, and streaming Olmo3Moe HF interchange for RL adapters.
23	  Custom objectives reject auxiliary-loss-free balancing routers with `bias_gamma` set,
24	  and optionally reset auxiliary metrics before training and on exit.
25	- Added an opt-in FP32-output LM head with low-precision GEMMs and mixed-precision backward.
26	- Added optional eager-rounding parity and dynamic-row specialization for no-gradient SwiGLU.
27	- Added `RoutedExpertsConfig.fused_no_grad_activation` (default `True`). Setting it to `False` makes no-gradient routed-expert forwards use the same eager SiLU-then-multiply activation as the gradient-enabled training path instead of the fused valid-prefix kernel, so policy scoring can share the training forward's arithmetic exactly. Explicit FP8 and wave-kernel callers are unchanged.
28	- Added `InitMethod.nanochat`, the nanochat initialization based on the spectral condition for feature learning: each weight matrix uses `std = 1/√fan_in · min(1, √(fan_out/fan_in))`, embeddings use `std = 1.0`, and depthwise convolutions use `std = 1/√kernel_size`. It covers attention, KDA, Gated DeltaNet, dense feed-forward, MoE, and OLMoDDP MoE-v2 blocks. The normalized transformer rejects it, since it normalizes every matrix after initialization.
29	- Added muP learning rates for Adam-type optimizers via `MuPConfig`, set as `mup` on any `OptimConfig` (except Muon/Dion) or on `OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig`. Each weight matrix gets `lr * base_width / fan_in`, embeddings get `lr * embedding_lr_multiplier`, and element-wise parameters get `lr`; parameter groups (including `group_overrides`) are split by multiplier when the optimizer is built. Use it with `InitMethod.nanochat`. `named_param_shapes` in `olmo_core.nn.transformer.mup` classifies parameters, and `src/examples/mup/coord_check.py` runs a width coordinate check.
30	- Added a base-model mode to `MuPConfig`: `MuPConfig.from_base_model(model)` stores each weight-matrix role's fan-in in a base model as `base_fan_ins`, and each matrix then gets `lr * base_fan_in / fan_in`, so every learning rate is exactly `lr` in the base model. Roles (`named_matrix_roles` in `olmo_core.nn.transformer.mup`) match matrices across models of different width and depth by block kind and path within the block.
31	- Added the CompletedP (Complete^(d)P) parameterization from "Completed Hyperparameter Transfer across Modules, Width, Depth, Batch & Duration" (arXiv:2512.22382). Set `TransformerConfig.completedp` (`CompletedPConfig`: `base_width`, `base_depth`, `alpha`) on the model to scale every residual branch by `(n_layers / base_depth) ** -alpha` and the `normal` init of hidden matrices, the LM head and in-block matrices with a fixed output size (MoE routers, KDA `f_proj_1` / `g_proj_1`) by width. Then set `completedp` (`CompletedPOptimConfig`) on `AdamWConfig`, `SkipStepAdamWConfig` or `OLMoDDPOptimizerConfig` to give each parameter group its own learning rate, AdamW epsilon and weight decay by role, width and depth, plus batch-size and training-duration scaling of those and of the betas. Supported for dense default / reordered-norm / peri-norm blocks and OLMoDDP MoE-v2 blocks. `OLMoDDPTransformerBlock` now accepts `attention_residual_alpha` and `feed_forward_residual_alpha`, and folds them into the branch output norm's gains when it can (`LayerNorm.output_scale`, supported by `LayerNorm` and `RMSNorm`). `src/examples/completedp/` has a width/depth coordinate check and a hero-architecture check.
32	- Added `CompletedPConfig.from_base_model()`, which records the fan-in of every weight matrix of the base model (`CompletedPConfig.base_block_fan_ins`). Each matrix's width ratio is then its fan-in over the same matrix's fan-in in the base model, instead of over `base_width`, so the base model gets exactly the base init and hyperparameters, including matrices whose fan-in isn't `d_model` (e.g. an MLP's down projection). Configs without `base_block_fan_ins` keep the previous rule and log a warning.
33	- Added `CompletedPConfig.fixed_kv_width` (default off). When set, softmax attention's `w_k` and `w_v` are readout matrices, with the output-weight init and epsilon, for models whose key/value width (`n_kv_heads * head_dim`) is the same at every size.
34	
35	### Fixed
36	
37	- The extra token rows of `SplitVocabEmbedding` (`TransformerConfig.n_extra_vocab > 0`) are now initialized by the model's init method like the base rows, instead of always with `init_std`, so they start at the same scale under `nanochat`, `llama`, `llama_depth`, `fan_in` and `normalized` init. The `normal` init is unchanged. muP and CompletedP now classify both rows as embeddings instead of raising.
38	- Fixed int32 pointer-offset overflow in the valid-prefix SwiGLU Triton kernels (forward, dynamic-row forward, and backward). Row and column indices are widened to int64 before stride multiplication, so no-gradient MoE activation buffers with 2^31 or more elements (for example 1,048,576 rows by 2,048 BF16 columns) no longer read or write wrapped addresses.
39	- Activation checkpointing now preserves the RNG state across recomputation whenever dropout is active (including `ResidualStream.masked_dropout`), so the recomputed forward replays the same dropout masks as the original forward instead of drawing new ones. Previously this was done only for EMO routing.
40	- Preserve OLMoDDP inference rounding in newly exported HF models, including packed dense/shared projections, packed SwiGLU, and architecture-specific BF16 TransformerEngine index-map combination; serialize the mode and retain legacy HF configs' existing numerics. CUDA inference without Triton uses the Torch activation fallback.
41	- Allow experiment workloads to configure the distributed timeout for long rank-zero dataset preparation while preserving the 15-minute default.
42	- Preserve 16-byte parameter alignment in OLMoDDP flat model buffers so compiled kernels remain valid after small BF16 parameters are packed.
43	- Keep no-EP and rowwise-NVSHMEM shared-expert CUDA stream switching outside compiled graphs to avoid Torch 2.13 backward failures after a separately compiled loss, while retaining compiled expert math and stream overlap.
44	- Metadata-backed packed datasets now include sidecar content hashes in packing-cache keys and dataset fingerprints, invalidating stale boundaries even after same-size corrections. Document lengths preserve EOS/BOS padding segmentation. Local array-backed defaults are unchanged (https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/pull/843).
45	
46	
47	
48	## [v3.0.0](https://github.com/allenai/Olmo-core/releases/tag/v3.0.0) - 2026-09-30
49	
50	### Added
51	
52	- Added `use_array_if_local` to `pack_documents_into_instances`, `segment_documents_into_instances`, `NumpyPackedFSLDataset` and `NumpyPackedFSLDatasetConfig`, forwarded to `iter_document_indices`. Set it to `False` to take document boundaries from the source metadata file instead of inferring them by scanning the token array for the EOS token. Inferring is only correct when every document is EOS-terminated: a producer that truncates documents and drops the terminator with the tail causes the affected document to merge with the one after it, and `LongDocStrategy.truncate` then keeps only the head of the merged span, so the following document never reaches training. Measured on an SFT cache, 97.98% of tokens reached instances via the inferred path versus 100.00% via the metadata file, with an identical maximum document length. Whenever the metadata boundaries are the effective source -- set explicitly, or because the source is a URL, for which `iter_document_indices` always reads the metadata -- `doc_lens` is derived from them rather than by rescanning the packed tokens for EOS, so the block-diagonal attention mask cannot merge an unterminated document into the one after it. The hazard is now documented on `iter_document_indices`. Default behavior is unchanged.
53	- Added opt-in paired SwiGLU backward and BF16-rounded weight-gradient accumulation for OLMoDDP experts, including Torch 2.13 support, checkpoint/recomputation coverage, and explicit backend and bucket-ownership guards.
54	- Added independent per-head Q/K norm gains and scalable softmax, EMO document-pool routing/global load balancing, and opt-in FP32 gradient-accumulation/reduce-scatter fast paths with explicit hardware/version guards.
55	- Extended hybrid MoE HF export for KDA, optional EMO and latent experts, per-head normalization gains, and scalable softmax, with exact tensor round-trip validation and legacy configuration migration.
56	- Added an optional, dependency-free checkpoint-ready notification callback for independent upload services. It does not upload or delete checkpoints.
57	
58	### Removed
59	
60	- Removed the `src/scripts/train/private-olmo.py` training script.
61	
62	- Removed the `olmo_core.model_ladder` API, its internal CLI wrapper, all eleven ladder training scripts (including the standalone Gemma-like ladder), two Slurm launchers, and the API documentation. Existing ladder orchestration configs and commands require an earlier revision; this does not change the model or optimizer checkpoint formats. The internal experiment framework remains available.
63	
64	### Fixed
65	
66	- Apply opt-in Q/K gain expansion to eval-only and model-only DDP checkpoint loads, and reject forced expert assignments and biased KDA convolutions during HF export.
67	- Validate normalization throughout MoE HF exports, preserve attention-only gates and resolved EOS/padding IDs, and reject unsupported shared-expert routing before conversion.
68	- Reject MoE HF exports with incompatible Q/K normalization or inconsistent KDA output-norm epsilons instead of silently changing normalization behavior.
69	- Preserve the resolved tokenizer BOS ID in exported model and generation configs, including when the training config leaves BOS unspecified.
70	- Reject hybrid KDA HF exports with sliding-window attention and EMO exports with restricted evaluation pools in any routed layer. Disable scalable-softmax HF generation caching and reject explicit cache use.
71	- Require the CUDA 13 CuTe compiler for experimental KDA, report incompatible installs before training, and exercise the kernels in a dedicated Blackwell CI job.
72	- Keep legacy fused attention configs compatible when the new attention options are disabled. Reject unsupported scalable-softmax context parallelism and KV caching at setup.
73	- Assign EOS tokens to their preceding document for EMO routing, matching attention document boundaries.
74	- Preserve serialized tokenizer behavior during HF export, including source BOS settings when the training config leaves BOS unspecified.
75	- Preserve FP32 router probabilities and accumulation when combining BF16 experts in the HF reference model.
76	- Avoid graph breaks from no-op profiling decorators, including compiled router load-balancing collectives.
77	
78	- Fixed tensor-parallel cross-entropy loss returning a rank-local partial sum instead of the replicated global loss. Mean reduction now uses the global valid-token count, including when ignored tokens are unevenly distributed across shards. The corrected reference-loss assertion covers sum, mean, and unreduced losses, with and without normalization and z-loss.
79	
80	- `dispatch_flash_attn_4` passed `cu_seqlens_q`, `cu_seqlens_k`, `max_seqlen_q` and `max_seqlen_k` positionally. flash-attn 4 inserted a `qv` parameter at position 3 (present from ~`4.0.0b19` onward), which shifts every following argument by one, so `max_seqlen_q` — an `int` — lands where `cu_seqlens_k` is expected and the call fails with `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'shape'`. These are now passed by keyword; the parameter names are unchanged across flash-attn 4 releases, so this is correct against both old and new versions. Only reachable on Blackwell, where `has_flash_attn_4()` returns True.

--- AGENTS.md ---
## Overview

Olmo-core is AI2's training library for the Open Language Model (OLMo) series. It provides modular components for transformer architectures, distributed training, data loading, and evaluation.
```

**How launch works**: When a training script uses the `launch` command (or `BeakerLaunchConfig.launch()`), it creates a Gantry recipe that:
1. Starts a container from a pre-built Beaker image (default: `OLMoCoreBeakerImage.stable` in `src/olmo_core/launch/beaker.py`)
2. Clones the git repo at the current commit into the container (requires clean working tree unless `allow_dirty=True`)
3. Installs the package from source (`pip install -e .`)
4. Runs the training command, optionally wrapped with `torchrun` for multi-GPU/multi-node

Pre-built images are listed in the `OLMoCoreBeakerImage` enum in `src/olmo_core/launch/beaker.py`, tagged by torch version and CUDA version (e.g., `tch2100cu128`). The `stable` image tracks the default torch/CUDA versions. When updating default images, also update `.github/workflows/main.yml`.

`BeakerLaunchConfig` also supports `pre_setup` and `post_setup` hooks for running commands before/after the package install step, Weka bucket mounts, and multi-node settings (replicas, leader selection, host networking).

## Testing

- Tests in `src/test/` mirror the source structure.
- Name individual test functions `test_*` and prefer `pytest.mark.parametrize` to cover multiple inputs or configurations without duplicating code.
- GPU tests use `@pytest.mark.gpu` and are skipped without a GPU.
- Distributed tests use helpers in `src/olmo_core/testing/distributed.py`.
--- pyproject L6 ---
name = "ai2-olmo-core"
--- pyproject extras range ---
36:[project.optional-dependencies]
37:dev = [
61:beaker = ["beaker-py>=2.5.4,<3.0", "beaker-gantry>=3.4.3,<4.0", "GitPython>=3.0,<4.0", "google-cloud-compute"]
88:torchao = ["torchao==0.15.0"]
90:wandb = ["wandb"]
91:all = ["ai2-olmo-core[dev,beaker,comet,dion,eval,fa4,fla,profiling,torchao,transformers,wandb]"]
--- version.py ---
_MAJOR = "3"
_MINOR = "0"
_PATCH = "0"
_SUFFIX = ""

--- AGENTS.md ---
## Overview

Olmo-core is AI2's training library for the Open Language Model (OLMo) series. It provides modular components for transformer architectures, distributed training, data loading, and evaluation.
```

**How launch works**: When a training script uses the `launch` command (or `BeakerLaunchConfig.launch()`), it creates a Gantry recipe that:
1. Starts a container from a pre-built Beaker image (default: `OLMoCoreBeakerImage.stable` in `src/olmo_core/launch/beaker.py`)
2. Clones the git repo at the current commit into the container (requires clean working tree unless `allow_dirty=True`)
3. Installs the package from source (`pip install -e .`)
4. Runs the training command, optionally wrapped with `torchrun` for multi-GPU/multi-node

Pre-built images are listed in the `OLMoCoreBeakerImage` enum in `src/olmo_core/launch/beaker.py`, tagged by torch version and CUDA version (e.g., `tch2100cu128`). The `stable` image tracks the default torch/CUDA versions. When updating default images, also update `.github/workflows/main.yml`.

`BeakerLaunchConfig` also supports `pre_setup` and `post_setup` hooks for running commands before/after the package install step, Weka bucket mounts, and multi-node settings (replicas, leader selection, host networking).

## Testing

- Tests in `src/test/` mirror the source structure.
- Name individual test functions `test_*` and prefer `pytest.mark.parametrize` to cover multiple inputs or configurations without duplicating code.
- GPU tests use `@pytest.mark.gpu` and are skipped without a GPU.
- Distributed tests use helpers in `src/olmo_core/testing/distributed.py`.
